 Judgment

Though the matter is slated for further orders, by the consent of learned counsel for both the sides,
the same is taken up for final disposal and heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent.
2. This is an appeal arising out of the judgment and award in MVC No.553/2017 rendered by the 23rd Additional Small Causes Judge, Court of Small Causes and MACT, Bengaluru dated 16-10-2018.

sentences.text:
3. The case of the petitioner/appellant was that on 23-6-2017 at about 7.30 p.m. while he was proceeding on his bike bearing Reg.No.TN.70.Q. 6619 on service road on Hosur-Bengaluru NH-7,
near Lakshmish Bar, Bommasandra, a BMTC bus bearing No.KA.01.FA.2064 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle resulting in injuries to the petitioner.

Immediately, he was shifted to NC: 2023:KHC:21348 Sparsh Hospital, wherein, he was operated and treated as he has sustained degloving injury to the right leg with skin loss and compound traumatic dislocation of left ankle.
and he has spent a sum of `5,00,000/- towards treatment and medicine.

It was contended by the petitioner that he was working in a private company and earning `15,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and therefore, the respondent being the RC owner liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent BMTC appeared before the Tribunal through its counsel and filed objections contending that there was no such rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus, but it was due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.

It was contended that the petitioner tried to over take the bus from wrong side and dashed against the pedestrian who was crossing the road and as a result, he rubbed against the bus which caused him to fall down.
Therefore, denying the negligence on the part of the driver of BMTC bus, it resisted the claim petition.
On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and the petitioner was examined as PW1 and Exs.
P1 to 13 were marked.
The Doctor who assessed the disability was examined as PW2 and Exs.P14 and 15 were marked.
The driver of the BMTC bus was examined as RW1 and Ex.R1 and 2 were marked.

6. After hearing both the sides, the Tribunal held that the petitioner is entitled for a compensation of `6,12,213/- under the following heads:

2 1. Pain & Suffering ` 40,000/-
2. Medical expenses ` 2,68,853/-
3. Loss of income during laid up period ` 16,000/-
4. Loss of future income ` 2,07,360/-
5. Loss of future amenities and ` 20,000/-
happiness 6.

Attendant, conveyance, food and ` 20,000/-
nourishment charges 7. Future Medical expenses ` 40,000/-
It also came to the conclusion that the petitioner had also contributed 50% of the negligence and therefore, ordered half of the compensation i.e. `3,06,106/- to be paid to him.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal.
8. On issuance of notice, respondent-BMTC appeared through its counsel before this Court.
9. The appellant has also filed IA No.1/2019 for condonation of delay of 7 days in filing the appeal.
The reasons shown in the accompanying affidavit sufficiently explains the delay and therefore the application is allowed and the delay of 07 days in filing the appeal is condoned.

10 . Learned counsel appearing for the appellant contends that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of pain and suffering, loss of income during the laid up period, loss of future income, loss of amenities in life are not proper and they are abysmally low and he also contends that the fastening of the contributory negligence to the extent of 50% on the appellant/
petitioner is erroneous.
He contends that the Tribunal has not properly assessed the compensation and therefore, the assessment of compensation be made afresh.

11. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BMTC submits that the Tribunal has sufficiently and properly assessed the compensation and there is no requirement for enhancement of the same.
12. The petitioner has contended that he had sustained degloving injury of the right leg with skin loss and compound traumatic dislocation of the left ankle.
Apart from that, he had certain abrasive injuries also.
The petitioner contends that there was no such negligence on the part of the petitioner and it was due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.

But it was contended by respondent-BMTC that when the bus was driven, the petitioner came with rash and negligent manner and tried to overtake the bus from the wrong side and dashed against the pedestrian and therefore, the Tribunal has fixed 50% of contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
The Tribunal also notices that the bus had not at all dashed against the pedestrian but it was the motor cycle of petitioner.

In the cross-examination of PW1, it was admitted that there was a complaint lodged by the NC: 2023:KHC:21348 pedestrian against the petitioner as well as the driver of BMTC bus and the Tribunal relied on the FIR produced by the petitioner at Ex.P1 which indicates that the petitioner being the rider was negligent in driving the vehicle.
It is relevant to note that the complaint filed by the pedestrian alleges that there was negligence on the part of the bus driver as well as the petitioner herein.
It is on the basis of this fact that the Tribunal has fixed the contributory negligence at 50% each on the bus driver as well as on the petitioner.
13. It is relevant note that the duty cast upon the drivers of the heavy vehicle is more than the duty cast upon the drivers who are driving the smaller vehicles.
In the case on hand, the petitioner was riding a two wheeler and the other vehicle involved is a BMTC bus.
The FIR discloses that there was an effort by the petitioner to overtake the bus and therefore, fixing the liability on the petitioner cannot be disputed.

However, the extent of negligence owing to the fact that the petitioner was driving the two wheeler and that the other vehicle was a bus and NC: 2023:KHC:21348 the apportionment in which the negligence is fixed appears to be erroneous.

Under these circumstances,
the negligence on the part of the petitioner is to the extent of 25% and that of the respondent's driver is 75%.

14. Coming to the compensation to be awarded by the petitioner, the above said injuries show that they were grievous in nature and the petitioner has examined the Doctor who has assessed the disability as PW2.
He states that the petitioner had sustained the physical disability of 43% to the lower limbs and therefore, the whole body disability is 16.3%.
However, it is pertinent to note that the petitioner has not adduced any cogent evidence to show his avocation.
Therefore, the Tribunal has considered the notional income of the petitioner and concluded that it was `8,000/- per month.

It is relevant to note that though PW2 has stated that whole body disability is 16%, the Tribunal has held that it was 12% and in the absence of any material to show the avocation of the petitioner, the same cannot be interfered with.
Sofar as the income of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has not led any evidence and therefore adopting the notional income has to be upheld.
The guidelines issued by the Karnataka Sri. Kirubakaran.

4
State Legal Services Authority for settlement of the disputes before the Lok Adalat prescribe the notional income of `11,000/- for the year 2017.

In umpteen number of decisions, this Court has held that the guidelines issued by KSLSA are held to be acceptable on the ground that they are in general conformity with the minimum wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner is accepted as `11,000/- per month.
Hence, the loss of future income is calculated as `11,000 x 12 x 18 x 12% =`2,85,120/-.

16. As a consequence, the compensation under the head of 'loss of income during the laid up period'
is considered for 03 months and as such, it is calculated at `33,000/-.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `40,000/- under the head of 'pain and suffering' and since there are two grievous injuries i.e. degloving injury as well as traumatic dislocation of the ankle joint, the compensation under the head of pain and suffering is calculated at `65,000/-.
18. Sofar as the medical expenses and future medical expenses are concerned, they are adequate and based on the bills produced by the petitioner.
Therefore no enhancement is required in the same.
19. Similarly, the compensation under the head of 'attendant charges, conveyance, food and nourishment etc., are concerned also, it do not require any enhancement.

20. So far as the loss of amenities are concerned, it is evident that petitioner had suffered the degloving injury as well as the traumatic dislocation of the ankle joint, these injuries are going to affect the petitioner for the rest of his life and scars due to the degloving injury is permanent.
Therefore a sum of `30,000/- is awarded - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21348 under this head instead of `20,000/-.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of `7,41,973/-.

1. Pain & Suffering ` 65,000/-
2.

Medical expenses ` 2,68,853/-
3. Loss of income during laid up period ` 33,000/-
4. Loss of future income `2,85,120/-
5. Loss of future amenities and ` 30,000/-

5 happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and ` 20,000/-
nourishment charges

7. Future Medical expenses ` 40,000/-
Total `7,41,973/-
Out of `7,41,973/-
, the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner being 25%, the entitlement of the petitioner comes to `5,56,479/- (`7,41,973/- - 1,85,493/-) which is the 75% of the award amount.
Thus, there shall be an enhancement of `2,50,373/- (`5,56,479/- - `3,06,106/-).
21. For the aforesaid reasons, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:21348 ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part (ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified, fixing 25% contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner and 75% negligence on the part of the driver of the bus and by awarding a sum of `2,50,373/- as compensation in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its deposit before the Tribunal.
(iii) The rest of the terms and conditions regarding deposit and etc., ordered by the Tribunal remain unaltered.
(iv) Respondent-BMTC is directed to deposit the compensation amount within four weeks from the date of the receipt of the copy of this judgment.

Sd/-
JUDGE Sri. Kirubakaran.
